title: How Dodgers’ aggressive pursuit of Tarik Skubal led to deadline stunner: ‘Skubal or nothing’
description: Where there’s smoke, they say, there’s usually fire. And on Saturday, as signs first publicly emerged that the Dodgers were making a move in the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes, the team’s...
fullText:
Where there’s smoke, they say, there’s usually fire.

And on Saturday, as signs first publicly emerged that the Dodgers were making a move in the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes, the team’s behind-the-scenes talks with the Tigers were indeed reaching a fever pitch.

A day earlier, the organizations had begun discussing a trade for Skubal — the American League’s reigning two-time Cy Young Award winner and this year’s top deadline target — in earnest for the first time.

“Right before the first pitch, I heard that it was pretty much done,” Roberts recounted on Sunday, as the rest of the baseball world was still digesting the Dodgers’ latest blockbuster acquisition. “There were obviously things that had to go on with medicals, so it wasn’t actually even finalized. I just heard that it was pretty much close.”

Over the next three hours, the Dodgers successfully pushed the deal across the finish line, ironing out a package that included three minor-league prospects — outfielder Zyhir Hope, and pitchers River Ryan and Brady Smith — in exchange for the majors’ most dominant pitcher over the last three seasons.

“Being on our side, you didn’t really know how long the process was gonna go, whether it was gonna go into Sunday, into Monday,” Friedman said. “But, obviously, we were of the mind to be aggressive and try to get a deal done.”

A day later, the reverberations of the trade were still rattling throughout the baseball industry, most of which had never bought the Dodgers’ repeated Skubal-related bluffs in recent weeks.

Though the team had insisted publicly and privately that it didn’t need Skubal, and that it wouldn’t make an all-in push to get the pending free agent at inflated deadline prices, rival teams always saw the Dodgers as his most likely landing spot.

The expectation was that Friedman & Co. would make a strong push in pursuit of a third straight World Series championship.

Friedman and Roberts effectively confirmed that on Sunday, saying the club had decided early on to target the 29-year-old superstar, whom they felt was the one true “needle-mover” on this year’s deadline market.

“Skubal or nothing” was the way Roberts put it.

“Our mindset,” Friedman added, “was we’re going to be really aggressive for one player.”

That didn’t mean the Dodgers were certain they would get Skubal.

As recently as the start of this week, it was unclear if the Tigers would even move their star pitcher as they began clawing their way back in the playoff picture. On Thursday, one team source estimated only a 25% likelihood of a deal.

But after Detroit blew a 7-0 lead in what became Skubal’s Tigers finale on Wednesday, a trade finally started to feel like an inevitability.

And over the next 72 hours, the Dodgers didn’t just hang around “the backboard,” as Friedman has quipped about so many of their other star additions over the last half-decade.

This time, armed with a war chest of prospects and few other roster holes to fill, they wanted to try to box everybody else out.

“With where our core is this moment in time,” Friedman said, “erring on the side of aggressive made the most sense right now.”

The first signs of apparent movement came just as the Dodgers began their Saturday night game against the Red Sox, when their Double-A affiliate in Tulsa scratched the highly touted Hope (who is the team’s No. 4 prospect and widely ranked as a top-50 talent around the sport) as well as fellow outfielder prospect Kendall George from their lineup.

Sources initially described that decision as precautionary — the Dodgers playing it safe with two young talents as trade deadline conversations intensified.

But internally, a Hope-centric package had already taken shape.

(An aside: George was also believed to be the subject of trade discussions the Dodgers were having with clubs, but a source noted he was also dealing with a knee issue, having only come back from a freak injury earlier this season).

At that point, the Dodgers were seeking medical records and doing “due diligence,” according to two sources. The Post’s Joel Sherman and Jon Heyman also reported that the team’s package was believed to be topping those of fellow Skubal contenders, including the Brewers and Yankees.

“Stay tuned,” one person with knowledge of the team’s plans said.

The Dodgers had maintained interest in other players throughout the process, according to sources.

One contingency was Mets starter (and former Yankees closer) Clay Holmes, who could have been a swingman for a Dodgers team that could use reinforcements in the bullpen. The team was reviewing reports for other pitching targets, too.

Still, Skubal remained their primary focus, with Friedman indicating the Dodgers never seriously engaged with any other teams about potential alternatives. And at some point during Saturday’s game, a final deal was struck including two young pitching pieces from the Dodgers’ well-regarded farm system.

That none of the Dodgers’ active big-league arms were included came as a surprise.

There had long been an assumption that the Tigers would want someone from their current rotation, with Emmet Sheehan coming to be seen as the likeliest candidate.

That’s why, when Sheehan was conspicuously absent from the Dodgers’ dugout during the middle innings of their eventual Saturday night loss, industry speculation piqued. It’s not unusual for starters to return to the clubhouse on days they aren’t pitching. But on this occasion, it fueled growing rumors he was headed out the door.

Instead, as Sheehan said from his locker after the game, no one had informed him of any pending trade situation.

Rather, the Tigers ultimately agreed to Ryan (the uber-talented but often-injured 27-year-old right-hander who has been sidelined by a hamstring problem in Triple-A) and Smith (a raw-but-promising 21-year-old flamethrower who has yet to climb above Single-A).

That rounded out what rival evaluators described as a modest — albeit, for what is still a rental player, understandable — package that the Tigers hope includes plenty of long-term upside.

“We gave up a lot of talent,” Friedman insisted. “Those guys are really good.”

But for what the Dodgers hope is the final piece of their three-peat puzzle, they were more than happy to oblige for another marquee transaction.

“Whenever there’s a star-level player that is available that can really shift championship odds,” Friedman said, “those are the moments that we’ll be more aggressive.”

title: Arsenal Agree to Sell Christian Norgaard to Everton for £7m After Just Seven Premier League Appearances
description:
Arsenal have agreed a deal to sell midfielder Christian Norgaard to Everton for a fee in the region of £7m, ending a stay in north London that lasted little more than a year and produced just seven Premier League appearances. 



 The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported that the two clubs have reached an agreement…
fullText:
Arsenal have agreed a deal to sell midfielder Christian Norgaard to Everton for a fee in the region of £7m, ending a stay in north London that lasted little more than a year and produced just seven Premier League appearances.

The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported that the two clubs have reached an agreement in principle, with Norgaard set to undergo a medical next week ahead of the move being formalised. If completed, it will bring Norgaard back into regular contact with David Moyes, who is entering his second spell in charge at Everton after replacing Sean Dyche.

Norgaard joined Arsenal from Brentford in July 2025 for a fee that could rise to £15m, arriving with a reputation built over six years as the Bees’ defensive midfield anchor and captain. He made 196 appearances for Brentford across his time at the club, taking over the captaincy from Pontus Jansson in 2023 and leading the side 68 times across all competitions.

That standing counted for little once he arrived at the Emirates. Norgaard made just seven Premier League appearances for Arsenal across the season, totalling 101 minutes on the pitch, with only one of those outings coming from the start. His final appearance in Arsenal colours came on May 24 against Crystal Palace, when he played 45 minutes in a 2-1 win. Arsenal’s central midfield had grown crowded well before Norgaard arrived, with Declan Rice established as first choice in the deepest role, Martin Zubimendi brought in from Real Sociedad for a fee that made him one of the club’s most expensive signings, and Mikel Merino also competing for minutes alongside captain Martin Odegaard further forward. Norgaard was squeezed into a squad role behind that group, used mainly to give Arteta the option of resting Rice rather than as a starter in his own right. Arsenal’s decision to cash in on Norgaard with a year still to run on his contract, rather than let him see it out on the fringes of the squad, reflects how little he featured even in a season that ended with the club lifting the Premier League title.

For Everton, the move represents a reunion between Norgaard and Moyes, and a response to a specific gap opening in the dressing room. Club captain Seamus Coleman confirmed earlier this year that his 17-year Everton career will end when his contract expires, closing out a spell in which he made 372 Premier League appearances, an Everton record, and 433 in all competitions after joining from Sligo Rovers in January 2009. Coleman announced the decision in his own words: “After more than 17 years at this great football club, I’ve decided this season will be my last as a player here.” He added a message for supporters: “I want to thank the fans for their unbelievable support. I’ve always tried my best to put Everton Football Club first and you all mean the world to me.” The club has offered Coleman the chance to stay on in a coaching capacity once he decides on the next stage of his career.

Norgaard, who has captained both Brentford and been part of Denmark squads at major tournaments, fits the profile of a player capable of filling that leadership void immediately rather than needing time to grow into it. He has won 41 caps for Denmark and featured in five matches, coming off the bench in both knockout games, as they reached the semi-finals of Euro 2020, giving him exactly the kind of tournament experience Moyes has valued in previous squads he has built.

The move would also mark Norgaard’s fourth new arrival of an Everton rebuild that has been active if unspectacular so far this summer. Moyes has already brought in Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough in a deal worth an initial £16.5m, made Tyrique George’s loan from Chelsea permanent for a fee above £20m, and signed Merlin Rohl from Freiburg for around £22m to add creativity in the final third. Alongside Coleman, Everton have also let Idrissa Gueye and Tyler Onyango leave on free transfers this summer, meaning the squad Moyes is assembling looks markedly different from the one that finished 13th last season after he returned mid-campaign to steady a club that had flirted with relegation for much of the previous four years.

With Coleman’s exit confirmed, the captaincy itself is also unresolved. Vice-captain James Tarkowski, who joined from Burnley in 2022, has made 128 appearances across all competitions and was named vice-captain in 2023 and has often led the side through Coleman’s injury spells, is widely seen as the leading contender to take over on a permanent basis, with goalkeeper Jordan Pickford and midfielder James Garner also mentioned as possible alternatives, with Garner having started every one of Everton’s 38 Premier League matches last season and led the division for combined tackles, interceptions and key passes along the way. Norgaard would not be walking into a guaranteed armband, but a player with his profile, a former club captain who led Brentford 68 times across all competitions, gives Moyes another senior voice in a dressing room losing one of its longest-serving figures.

Norgaard fits a pattern Moyes has followed throughout his career. In his second spell at West Ham, he built a side that climbed from the relegation zone to winning the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2023, England’s first major trophy for the club in 43 years, largely by recruiting experienced professionals in their mid-to-late twenties rather than chasing potential. Signings like Tomas Soucek and Vladimir Coufal, who arrived together from Slavia Prague for a combined £20m, and defender Craig Dawson became central to that side not through reputation but through consistent, disciplined performances in exactly the kind of holding and defensive roles Norgaard has spent his career playing. Everton fans hoping Norgaard can offer something similar at Goodison Park have that history to point to.

The Norgaard sale is a minor deal set against the scale of Arsenal’s summer activity. The club have already reached an agreement in principle worth around €90m plus bonuses to sign Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who has agreed personal terms on a long-term contract, while also being credited with exploring the cost of a move for Real Madrid’s Vinicius Junior, as they look to build on last season’s title win, and selling fringe players like Norgaard for modest fees is a routine part of funding that kind of business. Having brought him in for up to £15m twelve months ago, recovering roughly half that outlay for a player who barely featured represents a pragmatic piece of squad management rather than a setback.

Arsenal’s spending on midfield alone last summer, capped by the Zubimendi deal, meant Norgaard was always likely to be squeezed out once he failed to force his way into Arteta’s first-choice pairing early in the season. Once a midfielder drops that far down the pecking order at a club competing on four fronts, regular football elsewhere becomes the only route back to relevance, and Everton’s £7m offer gives both parties a clean way to move on before the transfer window closes at the start of September.

At 32, Norgaard is unlikely to get many more opportunities to establish himself as a first-choice Premier League midfielder, and a move to Everton offers something Arsenal could not: regular football. His six seasons at Brentford, including the club’s first promotion to the Premier League in 74 years and the survival campaigns that followed it, showed a player who thrives on being trusted with responsibility rather than fighting for scraps of playing time behind more expensive teammates. Moyes has built his sides around experienced, disciplined midfielders in the past, and a player with Norgaard’s positional sense and leadership background suits that approach far better than it suited Arteta’s system built for tempo and press resistance in tighter areas.

Should the medical go smoothly and the transfer complete as expected, Norgaard will arrive at a club searching for exactly the profile his Arsenal spell showed he no longer suited: a captain-type figure who commands a midfield rather than watches most of a season from the bench.

For Arsenal, the deal closes a short and largely forgettable chapter. For Norgaard, it offers a route back to the regular, high-responsibility role he built his reputation on at Brentford, this time in royal blue rather than red and white stripes. Brentford supporters, who watched their former captain leave for a Premier League title winner only a year ago, will notice the irony in seeing him land at Everton rather than fighting for a starting place among the game’s biggest spenders. For Norgaard himself, the move offers something a title medal earned from the bench never could: a manager who wants him on the pitch every week.

title: Rams’ Trent McDuffie Makes Strong Impression on 3-Time All-Pro at Training Camp
description: The Los Angeles Rams gave Davante Adams another proven opponent when they traded for Trent McDuffie in March.So far in training camp, Adams already believes the addition is improving the way he prepares.Adams praised McDuffie after Sunday’s practice and described the two-time All-Pro cornerback as one of the best tests he could receive before the […] The post Rams’ Trent McDuffie Makes Strong Impression on 3-Time All-Pro at Training Camp appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams gave Davante Adams another proven opponent when they traded for Trent McDuffie in March.

So far in training camp, Adams already believes the addition is improving the way he prepares.

Adams praised McDuffie after Sunday’s practice and described the two-time All-Pro cornerback as one of the best tests he could receive before the regular season.

“I don’t know if I’ll get a better look than what I get from Trent out there,” Adams said in a video shared by the Rams. “It’s the epitome of iron sharpens iron.”

"I don't know if I'll get a better look than what I get from Trent out there… It's the epitome of iron sharpens iron." pic.twitter.com/igO9hFtl3o

— Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 2, 2026

The comment came after Adams beat McDuffie for the highlight of Saturday’s practice.

Matthew Stafford dropped a 10-yard fade over the cornerback, and Adams completed the touchdown catch in the end zone, via the Rams’ training camp observations.

The sequence offered an early look at what the Rams hoped to create when they added another elite player to a roster built to contend.

McDuffie boosts the secondary on Sundays.

During the week, he also gives Adams and Puka Nacua a solid matchup on nearly every snap.

SEATTLE, WASHINGTON – JANUARY 25: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams catches a pass in front of Josh Jobe #29 of the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter in the NFC Championship game at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images)

Adams made it clear that the value of the competition extends beyond whether he wins an individual rep.

He pointed to McDuffie’s understanding of the game and the conversations that follow their work against each other.

At the same time, Adams is difficult to cover because he can change the picture within a route.

McDuffie’s quickness and anticipation can challenge those details executed by the 33-year-old receiver.

Los Angeles has already seen the matchup move in both directions.

Adams produced the red-zone touchdown Saturday, while McDuffie made plays throughout camp and brought pressure on Stafford during the same session.

Earlier in camp, McDuffie recovered from a one-handed catch by Nacua and broke up a sideline target two plays later.

Sean McVay said after that exchange that the Rams wanted “good, high-caliber ball” rather than focusing only on which player won the drill.

For Adams, the matchup is especially relevant after another productive year near the goal line.

Repeated work against McDuffie gives him a chance to sharpen the releases and late-route adjustments that helped make him Stafford’s most trusted scoring option.

WOODLAND HILLS, CALIFORNIA – JUNE 2: Trent McDuffie #22 of the Los Angeles Rams listens to head coach Sean McVay during organized team activities workout at Rams Village at the Warner Center on June 2, 2026 in Woodland Hills, California. (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images)

The Rams paid a substantial price to bring McDuffie to Los Angeles.

They sent the Kansas City Chiefs the No. 29 pick in the 2026 NFL draft, fifth- and sixth-round selections in 2026 and a 2027 third-round pick.

Los Angeles also agreed to a four-year extension that keeps McDuffie under contract through 2030. He arrived with two All-Pro selections, two Super Bowl championships and the versatility to work across the formation.

According to Next Gen Stats via Rams.com, McDuffie spent 17 minutes, 26 seconds in tight coverage during his first four NFL seasons, the fifth-most in the league over that span.

Pro Football Focus gave Adams an 84.1 receiving grade, which ranked 13th among 81 qualifying receivers, while McDuffie earned a 74.7 coverage grade, ranking 18th among 114 qualifying cornerbacks.

Adams was particularly effective against the type of coverage McDuffie can provide, posting an 89.9 receiving grade against man coverage, the eighth-best mark in the NFL.

McDuffie can certainly present many of the releases, alignments and coverage challenges that Adams will encounter once the schedule begins.

The Rams will ultimately judge the trade by what McDuffie adds to a defense that needed a true No. 1 cornerback.

title: Packers QB Jordan Love Sends Clear Warning to the NFL

fullText:
Entering the 2026 NFL season, the Green Bay Packers and star quarterback Jordan Love are facing an immense amount of pressure.

Over the last couple of years, the Packers have had Super Bowl expectations. Unfortunately, they have come up short of those expectations come playoff time.

Last offseason, the team went all-in on pursuing a championship. The trade for superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons was supposed to be the final piece of the puzzle. Due to injuries and a Wild Card collapse against the Chicago Bears, Green Bay ended the year in disappointment.

Heading into the 2026 season, Love and the Packers are once again viewed as a potential Super Bowl caliber team. For them to reach that level of hype, they’re going to need Love to take the next step.

With that being said, Love spoke out with a clear warning to the rest of the NFL early on during training camp.

While there are many who question the supporting cast Green Bay has put around Love, the quarterback himself is expecting big things from the offense.

“We got Christian, J-Reed, Tucker, they’ve been here. Been in this offense. Now, we’re just building on all the little things we’ve worked on the past couple years. MG locked in now over there at X,” Love said.

Looking past the wide receiver and tight end position, the Packers still have Josh Jacobs leading the way at running back. His status is still a bit up in the air after serious offseason legal allegations, but is one of the best running backs in the NFL when healthy and on the field.

If the offensive line can step up and keep Love upright and healthy, Green Bay does appear to have the makings of a special offense. But, it will be up to Love to make sure that expectation becomes a reality.

Since taking over as the Packers’ starting quarterback following Aaron Rodgers’ departure, Love has been very good. However, he has come up just short of being great.

Last season, the 27-year-old signal caller played in 15 games. He completed 66.3 percent of his pass attempts for 3,381 yards, 23 touchdowns, and six interceptions. Outside of the completion percentage, those numbers were slightly lower than 2024.

During that 2024 season, Love threw for 3,389 yards, 25 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions in 15 games. He threw for 4,159 yards, 32 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions in 2023.

There is no denying that Love has legitimate superstar potential. However, it’s time for him to actually turn that potential into production on the field in 2026.

title: WWE SummerSlam 2026 Night 2 Results As Roman Reigns Wins Match Of The Year Candidate

fullText:
Roman Reigns beat Seth Rollins in the main event of WWE SummerSlam Night 2 in a love letter to the Shield that doubled as a match-of-the-year candidate. Seth Rollins and Roman Reigns had no shortage of Shield callbacks, but all of them landed amid a 12-year story of brotherhood, betrayal and bitterness. Reigns won the match with three spears in a row in a perfect singles match that had zero interference.

Seth Rollins and Roman Reigns are closer to the end of their careers than the beginning, and this was made very clear throughout their promos on Raw. WWE played on Rollins and Reigns’ Shield history, and the dubious statistic that Reigns had never beaten Rollins in singles action.

Roman Reigns’ Bloodline was an important side character in this feud, but many of Rollins’ taunts mirrored that of LA Knight, the presumed next challenger to a victorious Reigns who has spent much of his main roster run accusing Reigns and the Bloodline of using strength in numbers without fighting fair fights.

Though Reigns and Rollins have had many run-ins, matches and callbacks to Rollins’ treacherous act to break up the Shield, there was a sense of finality to their SummerSlam showdown in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

Seth Rollins faked out US Bank Stadium with the Shield open, which received a huge pop before it dissipated and turned into Seth Rollins’ equally popular “Burn it Down” theme. No longer wearing all Black, Seth Rollins returned to his colorful “New Orleans-style” gear. Michael Cole described this as a rebirth for Rollins.

Roman Reigns received a bigger reaction than Seth Rollins on his way to the ring as Cole talked about each man being a pioneer of this generation who wanted to shed the hate they had for one another over the past several years. Reigns’ famed 1,316-day reign ranks above only Hulk Hogan, Bob Backlund and Bruno Sammartino as one of the longest reigns of all time.

Fans went back-and-forth with their support for Seth and Roman before the ring introductions. The singing for Seth Rollins surprisingly won out. The SummerSlam Night 2 main event started with a long staredown and some trash talk between Reigns and Rollins as fans salivated.

Seth Rollins took the lead early on with several counterattacks on Roman Reigns. Wade Barrett called Rollins the historical ghost who has haunted Roman Reigns for years. Roman Reigns got back into the match with a drive-by kick. Reigns dumped Rollins into the crowd, and the referee used “a lot of leeway” to let them fight in the crowd well past the 10 count.

Rollins mocked Reigns with his Tribal taunt, but as he went for the spear through the barricade, Reigns caught him and hit a Shield Bomb through the Spanish announce table. Seth answered with a Shield Bomb of his own. Back in the ring, Seth and Roman barely beat the 10 count. Reigns was a hair behind Rollins, who caught Roman in a Pedigree for a nearfall.

Fans chanted “this is awesome” as Rollins went for another Spear, but was stopped by a Superman Punch for a count of two. Seth Rollins dodged a Roman Reigns spear and hit a stomp for a false finish. Seth Rollins hit a superplex on Reigns, but Reigns countered the roll-through with a Guillotine.

Seth Rollins escaped the Guillotine submission and ran into a spear from Roman Reigns, but Seth Rollins kicked out. Roman Reigns talked trash to a stirring Seth Rollins, calling him the No. 2. Reigns went back-and-forth, shades of Bron Breakker, and ran into a Rollins Spear for a nearfall. “The only reason you’re No. 1 is because they make you No. 1,” said Rollins to Reigns.

Seth Rollins missed a stomp, leading to a Buckle Bomb by Reigns and a stomp by Reigns for a two count and an enormous pop. Rollins brought up the Bloodline, prompting back-and-forth strikes from the two former brothers. US Bank Stadium was in a frenzy by now.

Seth Rollins bumped into the official and came back with a Dean Ambrose clothesline. Roman Reigns paid his own homage to Dean Ambrose with a Dirty Deeds. Reigns missed Rollins and speared the official. Rollins hit a stomp on Reigns as everybody was down.

Seth Rollins grabbed the fateful chair. Seth went for the shot, but Roman hit an uppercut, causing Seth to drop the chair. Roman Reigns grabbed the chair and Seth turned his back, inviting the shot. Roman Reigns tossed the chair aside, moving past his obsession. It’s time to end this man-to-man. Minnesota respected the hell out of this with a loud standing ovation.

The one-on-one brawl ended in Seth Rollins countering the Spear with a Pedigree. Rollins hit a stomp, then prepared for a top-rope stomp. Seth missed and walked into a pair of spears, but there was still no referee. Roman Reigns hit a third spear and the referee recovered in time to count to three.

After the match, Roman Reigns and Seth Rollins shared a fist bump, signifying the end of the Shield lore in WWE. At least until Jon Moxley’s contract comes due.

title: Opponent Preview: Vanderbilt Commodores
description: Vanderbilt is coming off one of the most successful seasons in program history, going 10-3 overall and 6-2 in the SEC while being in the playoff conversation the whole year. Head coach Clark Lea has built up the Vandy program into something extremely respectful, if not borderline borderline playoff contending – will need a couple […]
fullText:
Vanderbilt is coming off one of the most successful seasons in program history, going 10-3 overall and 6-2 in the SEC while being in the playoff conversation the whole year. Head coach Clark Lea has built up the Vandy program into something extremely respectful, if not borderline borderline playoff contending – will need a couple more years of sustained success to go that far.

In 2025, the Commodores finished 8th in the nation in points per game at 38.5 thanks in large part to quarterback Diego Pavia. Pavia was the engine of the Vandy offense and finished as the Heisman runner-up. 2026, though, will see a new signal caller under center. Most believe that true freshman and former UGA commit Jared Curtis will be the starter in Week 1. A former five-star recruit and Nashville native, Curtis flipped to Vanderbilt just prior to putting pen to paper for his signing. Curtis is by far the biggest recruit in the history of Vanderbilt football, who had never had even a top 50 commit prior to Curtis signing. Having already drawn comparisons from his head coach Lea, it seems that Curtis will indeed be the starter. Other quarterbacks pushing Curtis for the starting spot are third year quarterback Blaze Berlowitz and and Whit Muschamp, son of Will Muschamp.

Though the quarterback will be new, the main player they will hand the ball off to is not. Sedrick Alexander returns for another year as the starting running back after averaging 5.4 yard per carry and accumulating 15 total touchdowns last season. Alexander will likely be tasked with carrying a bigger workload in 2026 to ease the pressure off the true-freshman Curtis.

The Commodores did lose All-American tight end Eli Stowers who will now be catching passes from Jalen Hurts for the Philadelphia Eagles. Despite the loss of their leading pass catcher in terms of receptions, Vanderbilt does return their top wide receiver in Junior Sherrill who led the team with 800 yards through the air.

Even with Alexander, Sherrill, and more returning, the offense will only go as far as Curtis can take them. While an elite talent, it remains to be seen how well his game translates from Tennessee Class A football to the SEC

While Vanderbilt’s offense was putting up video game numbers, their defense was merely trying to do their part in securing each win, giving up 22.8 points per game which was 48th in the country.

The Dores return cornerback and Rome High School grad Martel Hight who led the team in interceptions in 2025 (he also added seven catches on offense, too). Additionally, Vanderbilt returns both of their leading tacklers in CJ Heard (safety) and Bryan Longwell (linebacker). Furthermore, their leading edge rusher Miles Capers also returns to add to his sack total from 2025.

All of this is to say, while Vanderbilt’s defense was not one of the conference’s elite in 2025, they do return a good amount of their talent. Clark Lea made his name coordinating one great defense after another, and he will have that side of the ball prepared to complement their offense in 2026.

As is the case often times when Vanderbilt comes to Athens, it will be Homecoming week of the Dawgs. As someone who holds degrees from both institutions, the game is uniquely exciting for me; however, make no mistake, I want Georgia to win by 50 every time out.

While I don’t think Georgia wins by quite that amount, I find it difficult to see Vanderbilt not just pulling off the upset but keeping it relatively close. The Dawgs are formidable in Sanford, and no one in the stadium, from the players to the fans, will make Curtis’ life any easier after spurning Georgia late in the recruiting cycle.

title: LeBron James Philadelphia 76ers Tribute Goes Viral
description: Philadelphia is already embracing LeBron James, with a new Sixers mural of the four-time NBA champion attracting attention in Fairmount. The post LeBron James Philadelphia 76ers Tribute Goes Viral appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Philadelphia muralist Bill Strobel appears to be behind the LeBron James tribute attracting attention in the city’s Fairmount section.

The completed artwork depicts James in a black Philadelphia 76ers No. 23 jersey against a red-and-blue background. Its signature, @billstro4_art, matches Strobel’s Instagram handle.

A close-up of the completed mural shows the handle @billstro4_art painted beside the image. That account belongs to Bill Strobel, a Philadelphia artist with an established connection to the city’s sports murals.

Strobel previously painted a Jalen Hurts mural in Fairmount before the Philadelphia Eagles’ Super Bowl appearance. The Eagles described that project as one Strobel initiated himself at Brown and Corinthian Streets. He has also produced artwork for Lincoln Financial Field and other prominent Philadelphia locations.

The attribution turns the Sixers mural into more than an anonymous viral tribute. It appears to be the latest work from an artist who has repeatedly used Philadelphia’s walls to mark significant moments involving the city’s teams.

The mural appeared less than a week after the Sixers officially announced that James would wear No. 23 in Philadelphia.

James, 41, joined the Sixers after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers. He described the move as the final major decision of his playing career and said the opportunity to compete for another championship helped lead him to Philadelphia.

That context makes the mural more than an imaginative picture of James in another team’s uniform. He is now actually a member of the Sixers, joining a roster built around Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

Philadelphia has not won an NBA championship since 1983. James, meanwhile, has won four titles across three franchises. Another championship would make him the first player to win one with four different NBA teams.

The finished mural presents James in a familiar pose, wearing his trademark No. 23 with “Sixers” across his chest. Its appearance in Fairmount reflects the speed with which his signing has moved from transaction news to something Philadelphia fans can see in their own neighborhood.

James wearing a Philadelphia uniform once existed only in mock-ups and recruiting pitches.

The Sixers pursued him during the summer of 2018, when a Philadelphia contingent met with his representative, Rich Paul. James ultimately signed with the Lakers, beginning an eight-year run in Los Angeles instead.

Philadelphia’s interest was especially visible that year because billboards attempted to recruit James to the Sixers. Eight years later, he finally chose the franchise, turning those old hypothetical images into reality.

That history gives the Fairmount artwork an added layer. It is not a fan campaign trying to convince James to come to Philadelphia. It is a celebration of a move that has already happened.

James’ signing immediately raised the Sixers’ expectations, although their championship prospects will depend heavily on health, chemistry and how their collection of high-usage stars fits together. The mural captures the more optimistic side of the moment: Philadelphia has a new superstar, and the city is already making space for him.

The players heading back to Toronto were not immediately revealed.

The move gives the Cubs an experienced arm for the stretch run after the organization made upgrading its rotation a deadline priority. Although Gausman has not produced his best numbers this season, his track record and ability to miss bats make him a potentially significant addition.

Those numbers may not immediately jump off the page, but Gausman has shown encouraging signs recently. The 35-year-old allowed only one earned run over 5.2 innings against the St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday. He surrendered nine hits but avoided major damage, issuing one walk and striking out four in Toronto’s 5-1 victory.

Gausman also worked six innings against the Boston Red Sox in his previous start, allowing three earned runs while striking out six. Across his final two appearances for the Blue Jays, he recorded a 3.09 ERA with 10 strikeouts and only two walks in 11.2 innings. The two-time All-Star has compiled 2,081 strikeouts across more than 2,000 career innings while pitching for the Baltimore Orioles, Atlanta Braves, Cincinnati Reds, San Francisco Giants and Blue Jays.

The Cubs entered Sunday with a 61-51 record after a 2-1 loss to the New York Yankees. They remain firmly in the National League playoff race but needed another reliable starter to strengthen their chances of making a deep run.

Gausman gives Chicago a veteran who can absorb innings, generate strikeouts and potentially start an important postseason game.

He also arrives with another year remaining on the five-year, $110 million contract he signed with Toronto before the 2022 season. Gausman is scheduled to earn $23 million in 2027, meaning this is more than a short-term rental for the Cubs.

For the Blue Jays, the trade signals a different direction. Toronto fell to 52-60 with Saturday’s loss to St. Louis and entered Sunday 13.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East.

Rather than holding onto Gausman for another season, the Blue Jays elected to move one of their most accomplished starters and add to their future.

The full return will ultimately help determine how the trade is evaluated. For now, however, the immediate message is clear: The Cubs believe they can contend this season, and they have added one of the most established pitchers available to help them do it.

title: Yankee’ Austin Wells pays in-game tribute on anniversary of Munson’s passing
description: Catcher Austin Wells pays tribute to late Yankees legend Thurman Munson by wearing vintage-style equipment on anniversary of his death
fullText:
Yankee’ Austin Wells pays in-game tribute on anniversary of Munson’s passing appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The New York Yankees were able to come through with an important and well-pitched 2-1 victory over the Chicago Cubs Sunday at Wrigley Field. That gave the Yankees a series victory over the Cubs as they were victorious in 2 of 3 games.

A special tribute by @wellsius16 #RepBX https://t.co/5oDlhT9kbE pic.twitter.com/IbqOpkxDRa

— New York Yankees (@Yankees) August 2, 2026

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Yankees catcher Austin Wells was behind the plate for the Yankees with ace pitcher Gerrit Cole on the mound. A look at Wells’ catcher’s equipment brought many raised eyebrows, because it did not have the modern appearance of so many at the position in the 2025 season. Instead, it was a throwback and an homage to Thurman Munson, the Yankees’ late and legendary catcher.

Munson was the captain of the Yankees and played a key role on the World Series championship teams of 1977 and ’78. However, he was tragically killed Aug. 2, 1979 when the small plane he was piloting crashed. While Munson has been gone for 47 years, his memory and his impact on the Yankees franchise remains strong. Wells’ paid tribute to Munson with the equipment that he wore against the Cubs.

Munson caught for the Yankees from 1969 through 1979. He was a seven-time All-Star in his career. He had a career batting average of .292 and he drove in 100 runs or more three times. While he is not in the Hall of Fame, many believe he deserves to be in the shrine.

More than the numbers, Munson is remembered for the fire he had behind the plate and his willingness to lead the Yankees into battle. He was always willing to block the plate and take the abuse of a runner crashing into him if it meant preventing a run from scoring.

He is remembered today as one of the team’s legends, and Wells was not about to let the anniversary of his death go without his tribute.

title: Wings use 20-2 run to close third quarter, romp past Sun 83-63

fullText:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Jessica Shepard and Arike Ogunbowale scored 15 points each and the Dallas Wings used a big run in the third quarter to cruise to an 83-63 win over the Connecticut Sun on Sunday night.

After a slow start to the third quarter, when the Wings had more misses and turnovers than points, they followed a timeout with a 20-2 run to close the quarter and turn a nine-point lead into a 72-45 lead.

The Sun went 3 of 15 from the field and scored just eight points.

Azzi Fudd added 12 points for the Wings (19-11), who ended a two-game skid. Paige Bueckers scored just six points, the fewest in her two-year career. With reserves playing the fourth quarter Dallas still finished at 48% shooting, making 7 of 18 3-pointers. Fudd was 4 of 5 on 3s and Ogunbowale made 7 of 9 shots with five assists.

Diamond Miller led the Sun (7-23) with a season-high 22 points. Kennedy Burke added 14.

Connecticut finished a six-game road trip with five losses. They were without leading scorer Brittney Griner, who missed her fourth straight game with a left knee issue and has missed 14 games overall. The Sun are 1-13 without Griner. Another top scorer, Aneesah Morrow, was traded to Toronto on Friday.

Without Griner, the Sun were outscored 46-24 in the paint. They shot 9 of 23 (39%) from 3-point range and 14 of 44 (32%) inside the arc.

Three bus loads of fans from Houston attended the game. The Sun will relocate to Houston next season.

title: WWE SummerSlam 2026 Night 2 results: Gable captures IC Title, Reigns retains against Rollins
description: Between title changes and retains, Night 2 of SummerSlam was filled with action.
fullText:
WWE certainly kicked SummerSlam Night 2 off with a bang as Kevin Owens returned to the ring after a 17-month absence.

With the crowd unglued from the seats for a majority of the night, fans watching SummerSlam saw several titles get exchanged, as a pair of superstars added two major titles to their resumes, and one of WWE’s most legendary feuds came to an end.

For the fans who missed all the action from SummerSlam, we’ve got you covered below with all the results from Night 2.

MORE: WWE SummerSlam 2026 Night 1 results: Randy Orton returns; Femi defeats Lesnar

What a way to start the night, as SmackDown GM Nick Aldis announced to add Gunther and a returning Kevin Owens match to turn this one-on-one between Sami Zayn and Finn Balor into a fatal four-way match.

Owens kicked off the match, hitting every man in his way, including long-time best friend Sami Zayn. In fact, during the closing stages of the match, it’d be Zayn who appeared to be closing in on a win until Owens landed a super kick, allowing the returning star to hit his signature stunner on his friend and land a pin for the win.

Now Kevin Owens has a date with CM Punk for the Undisputed WWE Championship, a belt that has eluded him throughout his career, and also reignites an old rivalry with the champion.

This might have been a swing and miss from Triple H and the rest of creative, as Baron Corbin, who recently returned to SmackDown following a brief hiatus from WWE, would take down the red-hot Trick Williams for the United States title.

Both men would exchange an array of blows. At the same time, Williams’ sidekick, Lil Yachty, also had to involve himself in some fashion until Corbin would duck a kick heading the way that would send the rapper through a table, taking him out of the equation.

While the referee attended to Yachty, Corbin hit Williams with the U.S. Championship to land the coveted “End of Days” finisher, ultimately spelling defeat for the former champion, ending his reign after 100+ days.

Once again, the women of the WWE roster put together one of the best matches of the night, filled with action, highlight spots, and concluded with Chelsea Green winning her very first WWE Women’s Championship as the Minnesota crowd chanted her name.

Both Lash Legend and Tiffany Stratton wowed the crowd with their athleticism, showcasing that the future of the women’s division is in very good hands.

Charlotte Flair and Jade Cargill allowed their current feud to interfere with the title chase, even with Cargill’s running mates B-Fab and Michin coming into the fray to attack the competitors of the match.

In the end, while all the women in the ring were laid out, it’d be Chelsea Green to rise up from being stuck in the ladder to win the title and set up a future bout with Rhea Ripley when she returns from injury.

A legitimate comic relief for the evening, Danhausen and Dominik Mysterio faced off in the first-ever Human “Monies” on a Pole match featuring brief wrestling between the two wrestlers before interferences from the “Minihausens” and JD McDonaugh caused chaos.

Mysterio appeared to have the match won after Judgment Day stablemate McDonaugh took out Danhausen and several of his minions, but in the mix of those “Minihausens” was legendary luchador El Torito, aka “Toritohausen” for the night, who landed a flurry of moves to help take out the AAA Mega Champion.

Danhausen then secured his climb to the top of the pole, where he’d secure a bag of human “monies” that he then shared with the crowd upon his exit.

Checking off a major milestone in front of his home crowd and putting on the potential match of the night, Chad Gable defeated Penta via submission to capture his first-ever singles title in his WWE career.

In one of the best payoffs in recent memory for the WWE, Gable’s story to the Intercontinental Championship is nothing less than gritty, as this was his sure-fire “thank you” from the company for the amazing work he did with his version of the Grande Americano character.

Embraced by Penta, his family, and the Minnesota crowd after the match, Gable was brought to tears, acknowledging their support and the hard work he put in to get to this position.

Talk about an all-timer, truly. The work Roman Reigns and Seth Rollins put into this match could bring a fan to tears. From heavy punches, Shield callbacks, and an exchange of finishing moves, this bout between two of WWE’s best was a true five-star classic.

The storytelling between the two dates back almost a decade, with Michael Cole on commentary illustrating it all during one of SummerSlam’s best main events in WWE history.

Without the Bloodline and shoving a chair to the side while Rollins’ back was turned, Reigns pointed to the center of the ring and let his former Shield partner know that he wanted to settle their feud once and for all without anything in between them.

Delivering three consecutive spears to Rollins, the OTC Roman Reigns finally put down his long-time rival for a three-count when all the chips were on the table, retaining the World Heavyweight Championship.

At the end of the match, Reigns and Rollins reunited with a fist bump in the middle of the ring, signaling a sign of respect after their decade-long feud came to an end.

fullText:
The Houston Astros are “engaged in ongoing discussions” with the Miami Marlins about a potential trade for outfielder Kyle Stowers.

With the Astros trying to make the playoffs this season in the tight American League West, it makes sense that the team is looking to bring in reinforcements at the trade deadline. If they acquired Stowers, a big left-handed bat in the outfield, it would surely help Houston win the American League West division crown this season.

According to MLB reporter Jon Heyman, the Astros and Marlins are engaged in trade discussions about Stowers with less than 24 hours to go until the MLB trade deadline.

“The Astros are among teams to inquire about Marlins slugger Kyle Stowers, and they are engaged in ongoing discussions with Miami. Stowers, an All-Star with big power, just might be the extra lefty bat Houston needs,” Heyman wrote on X.

The Astros are among teams to inquire about Marlins slugger Kyle Stowers, and they are engaged in ongoing discussions with Miami. Stowers, an All-Star with big power, just might be the extra lefty bat Houston needs.

— Jon Heyman (@JonHeyman) August 2, 2026

If the Astros got Stowers, it would be a big power move for Houston as they look to win the AL West crown and head back to the playoffs after missing it last season for the first time since 2016.

Overall, the Astros have a very good team already, but by grabbing a few extra pieces ahead of the deadline, it could help Houston make a big push to win the AL West crown and, potentially, even the World Series.

Stowers was drafted by the Baltimore Orioles in the second round of the 2019 MLB Draft. He played his first 2.5 major-league seasons in Baltimore before the team traded him, along with Connor Norby, to Miami for starting pitcher Trevor Rogers at the MLB trade deadline in July 2024.

Since coming to Miami, Stowers has turned into a star for the Marlins. In 2025, he was named to his first All-Star team when he hit 25 home runs and had 73 RBIs for the Marlins, with a slash line of .288/.368/.544 for an OPS of .912 and an OPS+ of 151. He also had 3.7 bWAR in 2025.

Stowers hasn’t been as good in 2026, hitting just 16 home runs with 48 RBIs with a slash line of .237/.322/.465 for an OPS of .787 and an OPS+ of 120. He has just 0.8 bWAR this season.

However, he is just 28 years old and, with three more seasons of club control beyond this year, would be a long-term piece for Houston.

Stowers has primarily played outfield during his MLB career, but he has played more first base this season, so perhaps Houston views him as a long-term piece at first base for their team once Christian Walker’s contract ends after next season.

Either way, he would be a big addition to a Houston team that is trying to get back into the playoffs after a down year last season. With the American League seemingly being wide open this season, look for Houston to make several moves ahead of Monday’s trade deadline as they look to try and give manager Joe Espada some extra pieces to help the Astros win the American League West.

title: Kevin Gausman trade grades: Who won Cubs and Blue Jays deal?

Bateman is the 21st-ranked prospect -- per MLB.com -- in the Cubs' system and is a solid hitter who doesn't have a ton of power. title: Cowboys Waive 6-foot-6, 250-Pound Edge Rusher Facing 3-Game Suspension
description: The Dallas Cowboys have waived free-agent edge rusher Charles Snowden, who is facing a 3-game suspension from the NFL. The post Cowboys Waive 6-foot-6, 250-Pound Edge Rusher Facing 3-Game Suspension appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys were willing to take a chance on edge rusher Charles Snowden — they just weren’t willing to wait for him to heal up as they try to improve the NFL’s worst defense from 1 season ago.

“The Cowboys have signed OL Sebastian Gutierrez and waived OLB Charles Snowden,” The Athletic’s Jon Machota wrote on his official X account on Sunday.

Snowden signed a 1-year, $1.075 million contract with the Cowboys on June 18 and was suspended almost 1 month later. Snowden was waived with an injury designation as he was dealing with a groin issue.

“Cowboys DE Charles Snowden has been suspended for the first three games of the season, per today’s wire,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on July 14. “Snowden, per the NFL, ‘is eligible to participate in all preseason activities, including games; his suspension will take effect as of the roster reduction to 53 players.”

He was arrested for a DUI in Las Vegas in December 2024 and pleaded no contest in January 2026.

“Cowboys DE Charles Snowden has been suspended for the first three games of the season because of a DUI,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account on July 14. “The news of his personal conduct violation was on today’s wire.”

Snowden would have been eligible to return to the Cowboys for a Week 4 home game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Snowden, 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds, started 9 games each of the last 2 seasons for the Las Vegas Raiders, with 67 tackles, 4.5 sacks, 8 TFL, and 11 QB hits in that stretch.

NFL draft analyst Lance Zierlein projected Snowden as a 4th-round pick in 2021.

“Versatile defender who has worked both open and closed sides as an even-front edge defender,” Zierlein wrote. “Snowden is a long, smooth athlete dropping into space or transitioning with change of direction. Lower-body anchor is an issue and he needs more play strength, but he’s usually first to land his hands and does an adequate job of separating and setting the edge. Despite having some twitch with his get-off as a rusher, he gets locked out of the cookie jar due to an inability to convert at the top of the rush with hand usage or go-to counters. However, he has excellent lateral quickness for use in twists and stunts and has surprising potential as a zone or man defender when asked. Snowden is an ascending prospect with Day 2 potential as a 3-4 outside linebacker, but his ceiling will be defined by whether he can add mass and improve his rush.”

After going undrafted out of the University of Virginia, Snowden made the Chicago Bears as an undrafted free agent in 2021 and spent 2022 on the practice squad for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before landing with the Raiders in 2023.

“Sources: The Cowboys are signing former Raiders DE Charles Snowden.” NFL Insider Jordan Schultz posted on X on June 18. “Over the last two seasons, Snowden started 18 games for Las Vegas — recording 4.5 sacks and 8 tackles for loss.”

Snowden is part of a group of new Cowboys being brought in to revitalize the edge rusher position after a complete miss in 2025 — a year that began with NFL All-Pro Micah Parsons being traded to the Green Bay Packers.

Along with signing Snowden, the Cowboys made 2 more notable moves at edge rusher. First, they traded with the Packers for former 1st-round pick Rashan Gary.

Second, they used the 2nd of their 2 picks in the 1st round of the draft on UCF’s Malachi Lawrence at No. 23 overall.

title: Caitlin Clark addresses Sophie Cunningham controversy for first time; now the media has a choice
description: Just last weekend, Indiana Fever All-Star guard Caitlin Clark was laughing and smiling with Courtney Williams and Natisha Hiedeman, better known as StudBudz, on their 72-hour Twitch stream for WNBA All-Star Weekend. Clark, the 2024 No. 1 overall pick, surprised them with pairs of the Caitlin 1s, her forthcoming debut Nike signature sneaker. Hiedeman and…
fullText:
Just last weekend, Indiana Fever All-Star guard Caitlin Clark was laughing and smiling with Courtney Williams and Natisha Hiedeman, better known as StudBudz, on their 72-hour Twitch stream for WNBA All-Star Weekend.

Clark, the 2024 No. 1 overall pick, surprised them with pairs of the Caitlin 1s, her forthcoming debut Nike signature sneaker. Hiedeman and Williams thanked her profusely and hugged her. Williams wore the purple Caitlin 1s in the All-Star Game, becoming the second-ever athlete to play in the shoe. Williams affectionately nicknamed Clark “The President,” likely to signify her overwhelming influence.

“I made a call to the President, and y’all see what happened,” Williams said on the stream.

CAITLIN GIFTED THE STUDBUDZ THE CAITLIN 1s

Caitlin: “Courtney’s gonna make shots from 40 tonight.” pic.twitter.com/yTw3HTiuXC

— correlation (@nosyone4) July 25, 2026

The week after All-Star Weekend, however, the Fever sent all calls for the President straight to voicemail.

ESPN’s Hallie Grossman published the Sophie Cunningham profile heard ’round the world on July 21. In it, the Fever guard expressed her opinion about transgender athletes having a right to participate in sports.

“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,'” Cunningham said. “I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”

“I’m very much in the middle,” Cunningham added of her political persuasion. “I agree with things on both sides, disagree with things on both sides. And that’s all I’ve ever said about my political beliefs. But people love to assume.”

Intended or otherwise, Cunningham’s comments set off a media firestorm and served as a Bat-Signal to the far-right. Organizations against transgender women in women’s sports organized “Support Sophie Cunningham” rallies at Fever games in Seattle, Portland, and Minnesota. Cunningham mostly wasn’t pressed to answer for what she started, but when she was, she doubled down. Clark was shielded from the media entirely.

Clark finally took the podium alongside head coach Stephanie White and fellow All-Star guard Kelsey Mitchell after the Fever’s loss to the Minnesota Lynx on Sunday, Aug. 2.

Predictably, the postgame presser opened with this question about how Clark and her teammates have navigated the pre-game demonstrations and outside noise this week.

“I think, for us, it’s not really a discussion we really have in our locker room,” Clark said. “I think it’s for leagues and the governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions, but our focus is on basketball. That’s what we talk about and how we can get wins, and, obviously, we didn’t do that tonight.”

A visibly exasperated Clark interrupted a follow-up question by saying, “I just answered for you.”

Ideally, as a face of the WNBA and leader of the Fever, Clark would have been front and center — leading vocally as naturally as she does on the floor, like Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve has done.

“I would encourage anyone to go and listen to Cheryl Reeve’s comments. Incredibly thoughtful.”

The ESPN on ABC broadcast addresses Cheryl Reeve’s comments on transgender athletes, her “Trans Kids Belong” shirt, and meeting with Sophie Cunningham.pic.twitter.com/83YKH6X9HN

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) August 2, 2026

I have been among the chorus begging Clark for bolder action and more definitive statements, especially when her Black, LGBTQ+ peers don’t have the privilege of sitting out such conversations. But to be fair to her, Clark has used her voice multiple times over the past two years.

On June 13, 2024, one month into her rookie year, Clark offered a strong statement against the influx of hate, harassment, misogyny, and racial abuse.

“I think it’s disappointing,” Clark said in response to a question from James Boyd of The Athletic. “Everybody in our world demands the same amount of respect. The women in our league deserve the same amount of respect. People should not be using my name to push those agendas. It’s disappointing. It’s not acceptable.”

“This league is a league I grew up admiring and wanting to be a part of,” she continued. “Some of the women in this league were my biggest idols and role models growing up and helped me wanting to achieve this moment right here that I get to play in every single night. Just treating every single woman in this league with the same amount of respect, I think, is just a basic human thing that everybody should do.”

And one month ago, in the aftermath of Alyssa Thomas’ controversial play on her that sparked vitriolic aftermath, Clark opened her media availability with a five-minute monologue that hit the same beats:

Lengthy opening statement from Caitlin Clark: pic.twitter.com/fLlwYmvFLy

— Tony East (@TonyREast) July 3, 2026

On Sunday, Clark kept her response short, but her demeanor said so much more.

Clark looked drained and sounded monotone. How many times can she say the same thing, only for antagonists to  make her their mascot anyway? It was the image of a 24-year-old with the world at her fingertips who doesn’t feel comfortable taking hold of anything.

Who we saw Sunday stood in glaring contrast to the playful, sarcastic Clark we’ve seen at other press conferences this season, like when she teased her signature shoe or shrugged off all her technical fouls. It was almost a different person than the one who giddily crashed the StudBudz’s stream.

There is the perception of Caitlin Clark and the reality of Caitlin Clark — the perception of the WNBA and the reality of the WNBA — and the gulf is widening by the day, as Jemele Hill broke down with Awful Announcing‘s Brandon Contes last week.

“Being there with the All-Stars, among the players, if I would have told you what the headlines were about Caitlin Clark and the league in general, you would have sworn they couldn’t possibly be talking about the same league,” Hill said. “You saw the relationships that she has. You saw up close, no, this league does not hate her.”

The StudBudz do it through Twitch. A’ja Wilson never advertises it, but she has an annual Pride Cake tradition for her teammates. Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers haven’t hesitated to use their platforms to surface real-life issues, though Reese has her own difficulties with how she’s been portrayed and how her words are twisted. Maya Moore, Clark’s childhood idol, left basketball in her prime to dedicate her life to activism. Advocacy and solidarity take different forms, especially in the WNBA.

Perhaps Clark hasn’t figured out hers yet, or perhaps this is it.

Dating back to her star turn at Iowa, Clark has consistently shown the ways in which she is comfortable wielding her fame and in what contexts she’s comfortable opening up to the media. Would a performative pounding of the press conference table be better, if it wasn’t authentic to Clark? At what point does demanding Clark to be someone she isn’t over and over again reflect the definition of insanity?

Of late, Clark has asserted repeatedly, “You don’t know me.” And it’s true, even if parasocial relationships claim otherwise. We have no idea what Clark does or says privately to with her peers. We only know what she chooses to share.

Clark will never make everyone happy, whether she stays silent or speaks, and the choice is ultimately hers on how much she cares to use her voice regardless of that burden. The media has a choice now, too: cover Clark as she is or cover her as it wants her to be. The former might get us closer to the truth, while the latter all but guarantees this toxic cycle continues.

In a July 21 ESPN profile, Cunningham commented on what she felt was necessary to “protect women’s sports.”

“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,’” she told the Worldwide Leader after being asked about the “MAGA Barbie” nickname some fans have given her.

“I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”

Local media approached Cunningham about the comments a few days later and she doubled down.

“I said what I said. I think it’s kind of common sense,” she said. “And I think I’ll always believe in that. I think it’s really important to protect children, and that’s little girls who are also involved in that category. I stand on what I said.”

Cunningham’s stance has turned into a frenzied debate, with people from all corners of sports media, the White House, and multiple head coaches across the WNBA weighing in. Fever star Caitlin Clark has avoided the media since the controversy began, until her post-game session following Sunday’s defeat to the Minnesota Lynx, when she was curt in addressing the situation.

“It’s for the leagues and governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. My focus is on basketball” Clark said.

Caitlin Clark refused to back Sophie Cunningham:

“It’s for the leagues and governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. My focus is on basketball.” pic.twitter.com/R7HfzZIKwC

— BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) August 3, 2026

Some of Cunningham’s staunchest supporters on social media were furious that Clark didn’t say anything in support of her teammate.

“Sophie backs you all day everyday … and you can’t hold that same respect with common sense? Hmmmmm. Don’t like this look,” one fan posted on X.

“Coward. Everyone’s so scared to fight back… I refuse to participate in their fairytales. There’s males and females. Point blank,” someone else added.

“Caitlin Clark bailed on the truth a long time ago. She’s not the hero we thought she was,” another fan added.

Considering the Fever lost 108-100 to Minnesota on Sunday, it’s probably for the best that Clark is keeping the focus on basketball, and with Cunningham only scoring three points in the contest, she may want to refocus on what’s happening on teh court as well.

title: IMSA 2026 Road America results: Wayne Taylor Racing snaps long winless streak in GTP
description: The team wins a chaotic six-hour race for its first victory since June 2024.
fullText:
Wayne Taylor Racing ended a winning streak of more than two years in IMSA Grand Touring Prototype, winnin the Motul SportsCar Endurance Grand Prix at Road America with the No. 10 Cadillac of Filipe Albuquerque and Ricky Taylor

In a chaotic race (expanded to six hours) Sunday on the Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin, road course, Albuquerque and Taylor delivered the team's first win in the top category of the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship since Detroit in June 2024. It's WTR's first victory since returning to Cadillac last year.

"Very, very special," Albuquerque said. "This is more than just a win. Super happy with everyone.”

Albuquerque took the lead from Jack Aitken in the No. 31 Cadillac with just under 90 minutes remaining and held on through multiple restarts as the race ended under yellow. The No. 5 JDC-Miller MotorSports Porsche 963 of Laurin Heinrich, Kaylen Frederick and Tijmen van der Helm finished second, and WTR 's No. 40 Cadillac of Jordan Taylor and Louis Deletraz finished third.

“Amazing day, it was a full team effort," Ricky Taylor said. "So proud of how the team has stuck with it and kept working towards this sort of result, and just very thankful to Cadillac for sticking with us through all of it. They've always had our back, and they've emphasized how it's one team and that support goes a long way to keeping our confidence because our confidence has been challenged a lot with the lack of results. So, finally getting a win and not just a lucky one. It was a strong performance all day, so we feel like this is something we can build on.”

It's the second win at Road America for Wayne Taylor's team.

“I just couldn't be happier,” Taylor said.“The last 18 months has been the hardest 18 months for me in motorsports that I can remember. I kept saying to myself, we all work hard, we've got great partners, and the drivers are all working hard. The most important thing was keeping everybody positive and keeping the passion. To get a win and a third just shows to me that our work ethic, dedication, and focus as a team has paid off. This is really great and I’m very happy for everyone."

fullText:
The Atlanta Braves have struck again in the trade market and this time, they are bringing a starting pitcher to town. According to MLB Insider Robert Murray of FanSided, the Braves are picking up RHP Tyler Mahle from the Giants in exchange for RHP Anthony Molina.

The Atlanta Braves are acquiring right-hander Tyler Mahle in a trade with the San Francisco Giants, according to sources familiar with the deal. Anthony Molina is going to the Giants.

— Robert Murray (@ByRobertMurray) August 3, 2026

So far this season, Mahle has put up a 5.13 ERA (125 ERA-) with a 4.38 FIP (108 FIP-) over 18 starts and 94.2 innings pitched so far with the Giants. He signed there as a free agent for one year and $10 million after spending a couple of seasons with Texas and he earned that contract after making 16 starts for the Rangers in 2025 (86.2 innings pitched) and producing a 2.18 ERA (54 ERA-) with a 3.37 FIP (80 FIP-).

Clearly, the Braves think that they’ll be able to get the version of Mahle who was able to do a very solid job of preventing Hard-Hit contact (in 2025, he was 77th percentile of all starting pitchers with 37.1 percent of his batted balls being of the Hard-Hit variety), so this figures to be a job for pitching coach Jeremy Hefner to bring out the best in Mahle while he dons the Braves uniform.

Considering that Anthony Molina hasn’t done much at the big league level for anybody so far (and he’s only thrown five innings for the Braves here in 2026), this is definitely a buy-low type situation for Atlanta. Either way, he’s a starting pitcher who’s been able to at least reach the fifth inning in 16 of his 18 starts — though he did have a wobble in his last outing on this past Saturday, which is when he gave up five runs in 5.2 innings against the Padres. He did strike out nine batters (and has a strikeout percentage of 22 percent with a walk rate of 9.2 percent), so there’s that.

Either way, he may not be a front-end type starter for the Braves but he certainly figures to be an okay one if Hefner can do a job and help Mahle cook on the mound while he’s here. I’d imagine that there will be more to come from Atlanta going forward, so we’ll see what happens next.

title: Pegula leads Eala as storms push Washington Open finals to Monday
description: World number three Jessica Pegula and rising star Alexandra Eala must wait until Monday to decide a Washington Open champion after thunderstorms postponed the completion of Sunday's WTA final.Eala ousted former world number one Naomi Osaka, second seed Elina Svitolina and defending champion Leylah Fernandez to reach the final.
fullText:
World number three Jessica Pegula and rising star Alexandra Eala must wait until Monday to decide a Washington Open champion after thunderstorms postponed the completion of Sunday's WTA final.

After waiting through a three-hour thunderstorm delay to start, Pegula won the first set 6-4 and Eala led 2-1 in the second set of the championship match when rain returned.

More than five hours passed with conditions remaining unplayable before organizers called off the resumption of play until Monday.

Also postponed was the entire men's final at the WTA and ATP 500-level hardcourt tournament, with 10th-ranked American Taylor Fritz set to face 19-year-old Spaniard Rafael Jodar.

The women's final will resume Monday at noon local time (1600 GMT) with the men's final not before 1 p.m. in Washington.

Pegula, who won her first WTA title in 2019 at Washington, seeks her 12th tour trophy and third of the year after Dubai and Charleston.

The 32-year-old American top seed defeated Eala in a 2025 Miami semi-final in their only prior meeting.

Philippines star Eala, cheered all week by a host of supporters, seeks her first WTA title in her second career final, having lost last year at Eastbourne.

The 21-year-old left-hander is set to jump to a career-best 24th in the world rankings.

Eala ousted former world number one Naomi Osaka, second seed Elina Svitolina and defending champion Leylah Fernandez to reach the final.

Pegula broke Eala in the fifth game, blasting a forehand service return winner, only for Eala to break back at love to 3-3 on a blistering backhand service return winner.

Pegula saved two break points in holding to 4-4, broke again when Eala sent a forehand long in the ninth game and held at love to capture the first set in 40 minutes when Eala hit a backhand beyond the baseline.

Players were on serve and in a changeover when the rain returned.

In 53 minutes before the stoppage, Pegula hit 14 winners to only four by Eala while both had 20 unforced errors.

In the men's final, Fritz seeks an 11th career ATP title and his first since last year at Eastbourne.

Jodar, assured of reaching a career-high 15th in next week's rankings, seeks his second ATP crown after winning at Morocco in April.

title: Braves reportedly acquire SP Tyler Mahle from Giants, further boosting pitching depth

title: Luis García Jr. says he is ‘both sad and happy’ for trade to Yankees

When asked after Sunday’s 2-1 win at the Chicago Cubs about a trade for García, Yankees manager Aaron Boone was not in a mood to confirm.

The Yankees open a three-game series against the Cardinal in St. Louis on Monday night. There was no official word on whether García would be with the team.

title: Man admits transporting Scottish woman's body in suitcase, Greek police say
description: The man was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, as well as robbery and weapons offences.
fullText:
Greek police say a man has admitted transporting the body of a Scottish woman in a suitcase to an abandoned building.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, days after she was reported missing.

Local officers launched an investigation with cooperation from authorities in the US, the UK and Scotland, and now say they have arrested a 26-year-old man - the BBC understands he is from Afghanistan.

The force said he was brought to police headquarters on Thursday where he "confessed to his actions". He was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, robbery and weapons offences, but the exact charges have yet to be finalised under the Greek legal system.

Police said Ross, known to her family as Lisa, arrived in Greece on 26 June and stayed in the Piraeus area until 10 July, when she left for an unknown destination in Attica.

After carrying out investigations and analysing video footage, police said they identified a 26-year-old man was connected to the case.

They claim he transported Lisa's body to the abandoned site in a suitcase and subsequently used her bank cards to withdraw money.

During searches carried out at his home, police said a replica pistol and a knife were found and seized.

Lisa had initially stayed in the area of Keratsini, 5.9 miles (9.5km) west of central Athens, with Greek friends.

She had told them that on 15 July she would go to Kypseli, where her "American friends" or acquaintances were.

On Saturday Greek police said they were fast-tracking toxicology reports in order to ascertain the cause of her death, potentially "in the coming days".

Test results can take anywhere from several weeks to a few months depending on the complexity of the case and the workload of forensic laboratories.

They were also looking to trace Lisa's American friends, who they said were also staying in Kypseli.

First Minister John Swinney called it an "absolutely appalling case".

A Scottish government spokesperson said: "This is an extremely distressing time for the family of Elisabeth-Jane Ross and it is important that their privacy is respected while enquiries continue.

"Scottish government officials are in communication with the family and with the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office to ensure they receive appropriate support.

"As this remains an operational matter for Police Scotland, it would not be appropriate to comment further."

This article originally stated that Greek police had said the suspect had admitted killing Elisabeth-Jane Ross. This was changed after further information emerged.

title: Suicide bomber strikes antimilitant rally in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 14
description: A suicide bomber targeted protesters at an antimilitant rally in northwestern Pakistan on Sunday, killing at least 14 people, mostly civilians and police officers, and wounding more than two dozen oth...
fullText:
A suicide bomber targeted protesters at an antimilitant rally in northwestern Pakistan on Sunday, killing at least 14 people, mostly civilians and police officers, and wounding more than two dozen others, officials said.

The attack happened in Kabal, a town in Swat Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, where demonstrators had gathered near a police station, chanting antimilitant slogans and demanding peace, district police chief Omar Khan said.

According to witnesses, shortly before the attack, speakers at the rally said that ensuring security and eliminating militancy were the state's responsibility. They also accused authorities of failing to act decisively against militants, saying residents wanted to live without fear after years of violence that devastated the region.

Bilal Faizi, a spokesman for the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial emergency service, said the attacker struck dozens of people who were chanting antimilitant slogans and demanding peace. Police official Omar Khan said at least nine civilians and five officers were among the dead.

Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the bombing, expressing deep sorrow over the loss of life. In separate statements, they offered condolences to the families of those killed, prayed for the recovery of the wounded and directed authorities to ensure the wounded receive the best possible medical treatment. Zardari and Sharif also said Pakistan's fight against terrorism would continue until it is eradicated.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also condemned the attack. In a statement, he extending condolences to the families of those killed and prayers for the speedy recovery of the wounded.

The Swat Valley was once a stronghold of Islamic militants who imposed a strict interpretation of Sharia, or Islamic law, before the Pakistani military launched a major operation in 2007 that drove them out and restored government control.

However, militants have resurfaced in the valley in recent months, fueling fears that the Pakistani Taliban are seeking to regain a foothold in the region. In response, residents have repeatedly staged anti-Taliban rallies to protest the militants' presence across the valley.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the bombing, but suspicion is likely to fall on the Pakistani Taliban, known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP. The TTP is separate from, but allied with, Afghanistan's Taliban rulers. Many of its leaders and fighters have found sanctuary in Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power there in 2021.

Pakistan has long accused Afghanistan's Taliban government of harboring TTP militants, an allegation Kabul denies.

Pakistan has experienced a surge in militant attacks in recent years, particularly targeting police and security forces.

On Friday, Pakistan's military spokesman Ahmad Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistan has recorded 3,145 "terrorism incidents" since January. He said Pakistan had killed 2,084 militants since January, while 819 Pakistanis, including soldiers, police officers and civilians, had been killed.

Chaudhry also said Afghanistan-based militants had carried out 28 suicide attacks in Pakistan since January and alleged that most were carried out by Afghan nationals or people associated with Afghanistan's security forces. He said the TTP and other militant groups were carrying out attacks inside Pakistan with the support of Afghanistan's Taliban rulers and Pakistan would continue to target the TTP and its support infrastructure.
